memos.scout:
The honest case for buying DUST now is weak, and I can't make a strong one from this brief.

The strongest points: 1,182 buyers over the curve, a low top-3 holder share (4.8%), a top-5 post-graduation buyer share of only 20.5%, and 307 non-agent buyers in the first two minutes after graduation. Those suggest broad participation rather than a single wallet pumping. The coin is alive, not a factory, and the 30-minute return is still +4.6%.

Against that, the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (243.6) almost matching buy SOL (245.4), with 519 sellers against 644 buyers and a net flow of just +1.78 SOL. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.86 is high for an early post-graduation window. The coin is also 55% off its 30-minute high, and the momentum is negative. Bundle share is 75%, which is a red flag for coordinated buying, and a launch bot was present.

A 30-second execution delay and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost leave little room for error. A coin that has already dropped more than half from its high with fading buy pressure is the profile that usually keeps falling. The demand I can see is real in breadth but not showing up in the most recent flow.

Verdict: no honest case to buy now. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely way this loses money is a slow distribution into bids, not a sudden rug. The 30-minute high was 54.9% above the current price, and the last 15 minutes show buys of 245.4 SOL against sells of 243.6 SOL, a net flow of just 1.78 SOL: the buy pressure is already exhausted. The sell-to-buy ratio of 0.86 in the first two minutes after graduation and 519 sellers versus 644 buyers point the same way. Bundle share of 74.9% on the curve suggests coordinated early buying, and the completer share of 42.7% means a large slice of the bonding curve was filled by a few accounts that may be exiting. With only 95.5 SOL of pool depth, a 1.4-5.1% round trip plus slippage on a $20 ticket needs a move the flow no longer supports. Skip.
